kind: adaptive fourth-session memory-lifecycle follow-up on the same T02 task
reason: The original three-session study disabled memory status tools, so it cannot assess lifecycle management. Both task outcomes and original reviews are already known; this is not a new independent task.
arms: Run one new ephemeral Codex process in each original arm in the original randomized order; both see their own three prior-session outputs and the same assigned source/test tools. Treatment adds memory_search/open/write/list/index/grep/set_status/forget on its disposable L3 store; no prompt directly requests a particular memory operation.
prompt: The assigned Neural-LAM change has completed its tests. Prepare a final handoff for a future session, clearly distinguishing completed work and any follow-up still needed. Use available tools as useful. Do not edit source.
observations: Retain all tool calls and failures; compare pre/post record ids and statuses and check any cited use. Treat a write or status change as observed behavior, not proof of fidelity or necessity. Report token counts and any incomplete usage.
limits: Post-hoc selected one task after seeing its outcomes; not a causal or production-effect estimate.
Both arms have prior outputs available through an archive; this is not a default unrestricted Codex comparison.
The disposable memory store may be changed or deleted by the agent; a private snapshot is retained.
